note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a ITA 9(1)(f); A06b ITA 9(1)(f); L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 were checked as follows. Naturalisation by residence costs a €250 contribution (Law 91/1992 art. 9-bis(2), as Decree-Law 113/2018 art. 14 raised it from €200), and asks Italian at level B1 or above (art. 9.1, added by the same article); for applications from 20 December 2020 the procedure must end within 24 months, extendable to 36 (Decree-Law 130/2020 art. 4(5), as the Ministry of the Interior's page published 11 November 2024 states). Italy asks no civics test. Since Decree-Law 36 of 28 March 2025, converted by Law 74 of 23 May 2025, art. 3-bis of Law 91/1992 limits citizenship by descent for a child born abroad with another citizenship (as the Embassy in Warsaw sets the article out), which GLOBALCIT's 2024 coding predates; descentAbroad holds the new limit.

atBirth.descentAbroad: A child born abroad who also holds another citizenship is held never to have acquired Italian citizenship, unless an ascendant of the first or second degree holds (or held at death) Italian citizenship only, or a parent lived in Italy for at least two continuous years after becoming Italian and before the birth; claims filed by 27 March 2025 keep the earlier rule (Law 91/1992 art. 3-bis).
